PART 7 — TOXIC PATTERNS, COVENANT AND COUNSEL

Safety first. If you are in danger now: in India call 112 (emergency) or Women Helpline 181 (24x7). Child Helpline: 1098. Outside India, use your local emergency number. India's Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 recognises physical, sexual, verbal/emotional, and economic abuse. Men facing abuse can also seek counselling, police help and legal advice. Leaving can be the most dangerous time — plan with a professional or helpline.

7.1 The Third Person: Dividing, Helping, Protecting

A third who DIVIDESA third who HELPSA third who PROTECTS
Affair, meddling relatives, taking sides, gossip (Gen 2:24; Prov 16:28)Wise mentor, pastor, trained counsellor (Prov 11:14; Matt 18:16; Acts 18:26)Police, legal aid, shelter, helpline — in abuse (Ps 82:3-4; Prov 31:8-9)

Godly counsel is wise, trained, impartial, confidential, aims at truth/safety/restoration in that order, never treats abuse as merely "a communication problem," and never pressures the harmed person to submit more or reconcile quickly. Joint counselling is unsafe where there is ongoing violence, threats, coercive control, or fear of speaking honestly.

7.2 When One Partner Will Not Seek Help

A — Unhealthy patternsB — Emotional abuse/controlC — Danger
Criticism, defensiveness, avoidance → work on it: own healing, NVC, couple counsellingBelittling, isolating, gaslighting, money control → own support first, boundaries, accountability, protective separation if no changeViolence, strangulation, coercion, threats, weapons → safety first: 112/181, safety plan, separate, legal help, no joint counselling

Practical steps: get support and document; name it clearly with NVC; invite one small specific step (not "go to counselling forever"); set a boundary you will keep (your own action, not a threat); bring in trained people and separate if nothing changes.

Genuine repentanceFalse repentance
Owns it without excuses; accepts consequences; changes behavior over months, verified by othersApologises to end conflict; punishes boundaries; charm/gifts/tears then returns to the pattern; quotes Scripture to win

Limits: not everyone cruel is acting from low self-worth; some use power deliberately and feel entitled. Understanding wounds does not oblige you to be their therapist or stay exposed. Change must be chosen — "one who stiffens his neck after much reproof will suddenly be broken beyond healing" (Prov 29:1). Your own I-am-not ("I am not valued unless I fix this") may be what keeps you there.

Control, contempt, rage and entitlement tend to be Defender-style covers (Part 1.4); guilt-tripping, victimhood, jealousy and hot-cold swings are often Seeker-style. Everyone shows some of these at times — the questions are: is it a pattern, how severe, and do they listen and change (Matt 7:3-5 first).

7.5 Covenant: Should a Wife Stay in an Abusive Marriage?

No — the covenant is two-sided (love, cherish, honour, protection: Eph 5:25-29; Col 3:19; 1 Pet 3:7) and abuse breaks its promises (Mal 2:14-16; Ps 11:5). Staying exposed to harm does not repair a covenant; accountability and real repentance might.

Used to sayFuller reading
"Wives, submit" (Eph 5:22)Preceded by mutual submission (5:21); husbands must love "as Christ loved the church, gave himself up" (5:25-29). Submission never means obeying sin (Acts 5:29) or enduring abuse.
"God hates divorce" (Mal 2:16)Context condemns treachery against "the wife of your youth"; many translations read God hates "covering one's garment with violence." Ps 11:5: God hates the lover of violence.
"What God has joined, let no one separate" (Matt 19:6)Spoken to those breaking covenant lightly; Jesus allows an exception (19:9). Traditions differ; many treat abuse/abandonment as covenant-breaking (1 Cor 7:15).
"Pray more, be a better wife"Not what Scripture offers someone being harmed. Prov 22:24-25 warns against close association with a hot-tempered person.

Safety plan basics: copies of ID, marriage certificate, bank/medical papers kept safe; a small emergency bag; a trusted contact and code word; the nearest safe place/One Stop Centre; evidence kept (photos, messages, medical records); legal advice before announcing separation; children's safety considered. Do not tell an abusive partner you plan to leave if that raises danger.

7.7 What a Safe Church Does

A safe church doesA church should avoid
Believes and listens; takes safety seriously"Pray more, submit more, be a better spouse"
Separates safety from reconciliationPushing reconciliation while danger exists
Refers to trained professionals, legal aid, sheltersHandling abuse alone with untrained elders
Does not require the harmed person to meet the abuserJoint counselling/mediation in abuse
Teaches headship/submission in context (Eph 5:21-33)Using headship to justify control
Holds leaders accountable, with outside oversightSiding with status or a charming reputation
Allows a long, verified restoration processInstant forgiveness or quick reinstatement

Christ meets people inside their I-am-nots (Part 1). For those harmed, that means safety, dignity and healing, not more endurance. For those causing harm, it means honest repentance and accountable change, not cheap grace. Both are loved; neither is excused from truth.
